title: Week in Orbit
summary: This week saw a mix of strategic moves and setbacks in the space and defense sectors. SpaceX continues to dominate with substantial contracts, while Blue Origin's recent mishap raises questions about its reliability.

themes.title: SpaceX's Expanding Empire
themes.body: With a $4.16 billion contract from the Space Force for a satellite network and plans for Starfall reentry vehicles, SpaceX is solidifying its role as a key player in defense. Their ability to secure funding and contracts suggests a robust pipeline, despite the occasional turbulence.

themes.title: Blue Origin's Launch Woes
themes.body: The explosion of Blue Origin's New Glenn launch pad just hours after receiving a national security task order raises eyebrows about its operational readiness. This incident could have ripple effects on its commercial and governmental partnerships.

themes.title: Defense Budgets on the Rise
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adding $1.4 billion to space resilience indicates a growing recognition of the need for robust space capabilities. This influx of cash may also signal increased competition among startups vying for defense contracts.

themes.title: Emerging Players in Space Tech
themes.body: Startups like True Anomaly and Bellatrix are making headlines with significant funding rounds and ambitious projects. As the Defense-Tech IPO window opens, these companies could reshape the landscape, provided they can navigate the complexities of government contracts.
